chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who is struck by thirst to the point of fearing for his life, he said: 'He drinks enough to maintain his vitality, and does not drink until he is fully satisfied.'
ai.seo_question: How much should a fasting person drink when breaking their fast due to severe thirst and fear of death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the principle of proportionality in breaking the fast, permitting the consumption of water solely to preserve vital life force (ramaq) rather than for satiety (riwa'). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on avoiding excess even in permissible acts, ensuring that the exception for necessity does not become a license for indulgence.
